SK2150 A string search has an implicit culture policy

A string IndexOf, LastIndexOf, StartsWith or EndsWith call takes a string and no StringComparison, so the ambient culture decides where the match is.

CategoryCorrectness
Default severitywarning
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixyes, review it
Language version floor—
Since2.0
SupersedesCA1310

Why

SK2010 covers the comparison half of the culture question; this is the search half, and it fails in a way comparison does not — it returns an offset. A LastIndexOf("-") that finds a different index on a Turkish machine than on an invariant one does not throw and does not compare unequal: it hands back a number that a Substring then slices on, so the defect surfaces as a truncated identifier three call frames away. The ambient culture is a process setting nothing in the file mentions.

Example

Instead of:

var cut = key.LastIndexOf("-");

Write:

var cut = key.LastIndexOf("-", StringComparison.Ordinal);

When it does not fire

⚠ The method table is the framework's, not a guess, and most of `System.String` is deliberately absent from it. Contains(string), IndexOf(char), LastIndexOf(char), StartsWith(char) and EndsWith(char) are already ordinal on .NET, so reporting them would be telling the author to spell out the behaviour they already have. Only the four methods whose string overload documents current-culture semantics are inspected: IndexOf, LastIndexOf, StartsWith and EndsWith, and only where the first argument is a string. Any overload already taking a StringComparison or a CultureInfo is silent, as is any lookalike method on a type that is not System.String. ⚠ The fix is `fixIsSafe: false` against the issue's proposal. Appending StringComparison.Ordinal changes what the program computes — that is the whole point of the finding — and doc 08 reserves fixIsSafe: true for edits that do not. ⚠ The issue also claims this is "the same fix `SK2010` already emits"; `SK2010` emits no fix at all (hasFix: false), because for a comparison there is no way to choose between ordinal, invariant and user-culture semantics. Search is different only because an offset into a string is an ordinal question by construction. The inserted type name is qualified as System.StringComparison wherever StringComparison does not already bind at the call site, so the edit compiles in a file with no using System;.
